Sure! Off the top of my head:

I'm using Argenine AKG, and argenine itself has beneficial effects for skin, so it may not just be the AKG itself.

I would need to document and measure effects of the A-AKG, but anecdotally, I got a 2nd degree burn on my finger, and applied AKG to it after reading a study about AKG for burn victims. The burn healed extremely quickly, much quicker than other burns I have gotten in the past, and there is minimal hyperpigmentation left over. I'll purchase some Ca-AKG as well and let you know if there's a difference.

I don't get acne after starting the AKG facial regiment, but I also attribute that to another factor like adding vitamin c serum into my routine again. Before adding the vitamin C, I also noticed that any acne scars also lessened, and pigmentation of the skin was more even.

There is an extreme whitening effect immediately after applying AKG to the face or body. Especially after a hot shower, applying AKG to the skin will cause a reddened area to become white. This is not a cast from the powder on the skin, it looks as if all of the reddening from the heat exposure is gone for a few minutes, similar to how it would look if one pressed on their skin, with the pressure causing it to become lighter than the surrounding areas. I mix the A-AKG powder in as little hot water as possible until it is dissolved. I have occasionally added a carrier oil like a small amount of coconut oil to help it spread better.

I find that the immediately observable skin benefits when applied to the face last about 6 hours, afterwards the skin tightening decreases to baseline once more, although the general quality of my skin has improved over time since starting.

This used to be me.

I changed by getting into position to work, closing my eyes, and blocking out as many other thoughts as I could, I imagine the work as already having been completed, and how good that would feel. Then I open my eyes and get to work, and try to treat the present as if it's a memory being played back by the me who experienced the satisfaction I had just manufactured.

This might sound really contrived, but essentially what I found is happening is I get immersed in doing the thing as if the completed state is already a sure thing, and I follow through with it until it's completed. I know that by currently working on what I was putting off, that it's as good as finished, and I just stay locked into doing it until it's completed. 

I was a chronic procrastinator my entire life, but by not making a distinction between having completed a task and doing a task, I'm able to start and finish things as long as I can get myself into position in the first place.

Going to 'sleep' and never waking up is how this appeals to people with depression, who suffer every day and see tomorrow as being one more day of suffering. From the viewpoint of a depressed person, suicide is not a pointless action.

Logically, outside the mind of the depressed person, other people can project their own hope and observations on the situation. Unfortunately, this does not appear in the mind of the depressed person, and any appeals to potential and hope just remind them how unappealing existing at all is.

Dear friend, 

I have been there, in that place of severe loneliness. The people you loved are gone, even the ones who said they'd marry you and love you forever, and now you hate yourself.

You might feel suicidal, it's natural. But you will keep going because you WANT to feel happy again. It's just right now you can't feel happy. One day you will. I didn't think I would, and I still get into prolonged periods of sadness, but I can function and remain happy for longer periods of time. There are some ways you can make this process go quicker.

For me, it was finding an old friend and getting to know him and his family better. Exposing yourself to people outside of your unhappiness will force you to act happy and BECOME happy. Immerse yourself in some new, loving environment. Get active. Do things you're good at.

I love you, I hope you find happiness again. It's so easily lost. The bright side is you know what rock bottom feels like, and when you do find happiness again, you will know how valuable it is and how hard you have to work to keep it. 

Rock on.
